lines.text: Before a model can read your sentence, something has to chop it into pieces.
Those pieces are tokens, and they come from a tokenizer.
The tokenizer is trained on a specific corpus, so it learns what is common in that corpus.
Common things become one token. Rare things get chopped into several.
English text is well represented, because most tokenizer training data is English.
Other languages are not. The same meaning costs more tokens.
And that is not a rounding detail. Tokens are what you are billed for.
Same answer, more tokens, higher price.
You can see it directly. Take one sentence and translate it.
English takes a certain number of tokens. Another language takes more. A different script takes far more.
Which is a tax on every language that was not in the training corpus.
There are fixes. Train the tokenizer on more languages, or drop the tokenizer altogether.
Until someone does, the token count is not a measurement of the text. It is a measurement of the tokenizer.
